title: Welcome to Web Development
learning_outcomes: Structure meaningful pages with semantic HTML.
Style responsive layouts with CSS, typography and accessible visual states.
Use JavaScript fundamentals and DOM events to add useful interactions.
Publish and evaluate a small accessible website.
module_titles: Build, test and publish a website

sections.heading: What is Web Development?
sections.body: Web development is the work of creating websites and web applications that people use in a browser. Think of a website like a shop: HTML gives it a structure, CSS arranges and decorates it, and JavaScript can make parts respond to visitors.

sections.heading: Why is it useful?
sections.body: Websites help schools share information, small businesses display products, farmers reach customers, and community groups provide services. Web applications can also support tasks such as enquiries, learning, bookings, and online payments, including services used in Kenya and across Africa.

sections.heading: What can you build or do with it?
sections.body: You will create meaningful page structures with HTML, style them with CSS, make layouts work on different screen sizes, and add useful interactions with JavaScript. By the end, you will publish and evaluate a small website with attention to accessibility.

sections.heading: How to use these lessons
sections.body: Read each explanation, predict how a page or code example will appear or behave, and then try it in your own files. Complete the knowledge checks and activities, and test your pages on narrow and wide screens as well as with a keyboard.

sections.heading: What you need
sections.body: Basic computer skills are helpful, but no previous programming experience is required. You need a computer, a modern web browser, and a text or code editor; internet is needed to access online lessons and publish a site, but you can practise many activities offline.
